## New Learning: The Phonogram **eigh**

<div class="phonogram">eigh</div>

**eigh** says 1 sound: /ā/

EIGH is a four-letter /ā/. The GH is silent here (Rule 28). Think: 'E-I-G-H spells /ā/!' as in 'eight.'


> **Rule:** Rule 28: GH is often silent after I.

| Sound | Example Words |
|-------|--------------|
| /ā/ | eight, neighbor, weight, freight |

---

## Spelling Analysis

| Word | Phonograms Used | Rules Applied | Say-to-Spell |
|------|----------------|---------------|--------------|
| eight | eigh (/ā/), t (/t/) | Rule 28: GH silent | /āt/ |
| neighbor | n (/n/), eigh (/ā/), b (/b/), or (/or/) | Rule 28 | nā-bor |
| weigh | w (/w/), eigh (/ā/) | Rule 28 | /wā/ |

## Reading Practice

> eight &nbsp;&nbsp; neighbor &nbsp;&nbsp; weigh

<details class="teacher-script">
<summary>📖 Phonogram eigh — Teacher Script</summary>

> **Say:** "Today we are going to learn a new phonogram. A phonogram is a letter or group of letters that makes one or more sounds."

<div class="phonogram">eigh</div>

> **Say:** "This is the phonogram **eigh**." *(Point to the card.)* "It says /ā/."

> **Say:** "Listen to me say its sounds: /ā/. Now you say them."

> *(Child repeats.)*

> **Say:** "Good. Now let's write it. Watch me first." *(Demonstrate writing eigh.)*

> **Say:** "Now you write **eigh** three times. Say '/ā/' each time you write it."

> *(Child writes on whiteboard. Check formation.)*

> **Say:** "Every time you see this phonogram, you will try each of its sounds until the word makes sense. Let's practice with some words."



> **Say:** "What did you learn today?" *(Child responds: "The phonogram eigh — it says /ā/.")*
